messages:
sam: Heads up — saw OOMs on prod_1 during a canary when kernel_chooser picked the Triton path for attention at seq_len=4096. No config changes besides a small rollout. Logs show large workspace alloc before failure. anyone seen this? :eyes:

anya: saw something similar last week in staging. Triton seems to blow up workspace on padded batches. reprod ok with synthetic trace?

kevin: quick profiling snapshot (from local repro):
```
MODEL redwood-m4, seq=4096, batch=8, heads=16, d_head=64
flashattn: attn_ws=0.45GB, ffn_ws=0.18GB
triton  : attn_ws=1.20GB, ffn_ws=0.62GB
KV cache: 7.8GB (persistent per-request)
GPU free before: 10.2GB -> alloc fail when triton path tries to reserve
```

devin: that matches my hunch — Triton kernels allocate bigger temp buffers for tiling/padded tokens. Two levers: (1) dynamic workspace capping in kernel_chooser, (2) allocator reserve / slab reclaim for KV.

anya: +1 on allocator tuning. We had a case where reserve_pct=0.05 wasn't enough for sudden triton spikes.

kevin: thinking config knobs — propose adding triton_max_ws and prefer_flash_threshold. Example:
```
kernel_chooser:
  prefer_flash_threshold: 3072  # prefer flash if seq <= 3072
  triton_max_ws: 800MB         # cap triton workspace; fallback to flash or cuBLASLt
allocator:
  reserve_pct: 0.12            # keep 12% GPU as emergency reserve
  slab_chunk: 256MB
  enable_reclaim: true
```

devin: also want a lightweight probe API so we can estimate peak WS without allocating full KV. CLI: `./probe_ws --model redwood-m4 --seq 4096 --batch 8 --kernel triton` should return expected_ws and safety_margin.

kevin: I added a quick probe run — result: `expected_ws=1.18GB, worst_case=1.35GB (tiling overhead)`. Probe uses malloc-trace, non-destructive.

anya: note: prefer_flash_threshold interacts with quantized kernels; for some int8 paths flash isn't available -> kernel_chooser must consider precision compatibility too.

devin: plan: implement triton_max_ws cap + allocator reserve on feature branch. If triton exceeds cap, fall back to flash or cuBLASLt if supported. We'll also add a small KV reclaim hook: when free_memory < reserve_pct*total, mark oldest KV segments as reclaimable and asynchronously persist + evict.

sam: please add tracepoints for mempool.evictions and kernel_chooser.decisions. we need metrics for canary dashboards.

kevin: putting a small perf table in the issue for staging runs:
```
seq  | path    | avg_latency | p95_latency | max_ws_used
1024 | flash   | 45ms        | 70ms        | 0.12GB
2048 | flash   | 90ms        | 130ms       | 0.28GB
3072 | triton  | 160ms       | 240ms       | 0.72GB
4096 | triton* | 320ms       | 520ms       | 1.20GB  <-- OOM risk when KV present
```

anya: staging canary results will be noisy; include KV-on/KV-off variants.

devin: can add a lightweight fallback policy: if expected_ws + kv_estimate > gpu_free - reserve -> route to smaller-model or degrade to sampling-only response. (configurable)

infra-bot: deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-12T14:03 succeeded -> staging feature branch `triton-ws-cap` live on staging.

sam: Action items: kevin: run probe matrix [1024,2048,3072,4096] across batch sizes [1,4,8] and post numbers; devin: PR allocator + kernel_chooser flags; anya: run canary in us-west2-gpu1 and watch mempool.evictions metric; I'll open perf-issue and assign. :thumbsup:

kevin: starting probes now, will paste results in the issue.

anya: thanks — will hold canary until kevin confirms probe numbers.

sam: nice teamwork. keep thread for updates only.
